chapter: Herbie Harper and Rasch's notes on Johnson
title: 'One Day' and Berniece Johnson
summary: Harper says Johnson wrote slowly and that 'One Day' as sung by Berniece Johnson in the show made him cry.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: Some more comments from Herbie Harper, who was a colleague. He was the choreographer for the Jazz Train that toured, was in New York and also toured Europe, played before royalty, et cetera. Herbie and J. C.'s
relationship went back a really long time, and here are some more thoughts about working with him.

I think it took him quite a while to write a piece. Like in his poetry; it's beautiful; it's quiet. His lyrics to his songs are beautiful. And in fact one song called "One Day" -- it was marvelous at the theater, and I would anticipate a coming up. I would --

-- (inaudible) because when I read it, I would cry because it was such a beautiful song. And the girl that sang it, Berniece -- Berniece Johnson, that was her name; she was a church person, church woman with a beautiful voice. And in her voice was all the beauty of -- she was clean, if you know what I mean. She -- you think of a nightclub singer, you think of whiskey and dope and prostitution. But this woman and her voice was just, everything was just the opposite.
And when she would sing "One Day," she --
I know, there's something so beautiful about that song.
